v.why: With edge 4 absent, deleting edge 3 leaves edge 5 as the only path into the output (or none at all), so accuracy collapses (exps 4, 6).
In parameter-free, skip-heavy cells, removing the direct input-to-output skip pushes signal through deeper paths and improves accuracy (exp 9), whereas in conv cells it hurts.
Adding a 3x3 conv helps most when the rest of the cell lacks convolutions, e.g. skip-based cells (exp 19).
When the parallel edge 0->2 is a parameter-free skip, the cell has little learnable capacity, so a conv on edge 0 adds much more (exp 28).
Removing edge 5 when edge 4 is already none leaves at most the edge 3 path into the output, sharply cutting capacity or disconnecting the cell (exps 63, 64).
Deleting a 3x3 conv on the last edge loses learnable capacity, while deleting a skip or pool there is neutral or beneficial (exps 61-64 vs 65-67).
When edge 4 is missing, a conv on edge 3 restores a needed path to the output and gives large gains (exps 75, 78).
Filling an empty edge 3 adds a new path to the output, which helps far more than replacing an existing skip, pool or conv there (exps 71, 75-79 vs 72-74).
Without the input-to-output skip on edge 3, a skip on edge 4 supplies the residual path the deep conv cell needs (exp 34).
When edge 3 is none, a skip on edge 1 provides a shortcut from the input that is otherwise missing, giving large ImageNet16-120 gains (exps 57, 58).

Each hypothesis below rests on observed contrasts in the 100 experiments, plus known structural facts about NAS-Bench-201. Two of these facts matter most. First, edge 3 (0→3), edge 4 (1→3) and edge 5 (2→3) are the only routes into the output node. Second, cells made only of parameter-free operations train poorly.

| # | Edit | Condition | Direction | Main evidence |
|---|------|-----------|-----------|---------------|
| 1 | e3 → none | e4 = none | lower | Exp 4, 6: drops of −21.6 to −73.6 |
| 2 | e3 → none | e0 = skip_connect | higher | Exp 9: +29.3 / +23.4 / +3.7 |
| 3 | e5 → nor_conv_3x3 | e0 = skip_connect | higher | Exp 19: gains of +17.7 to +46.7 |
| 4 | e0 → nor_conv_3x3 | e1 = skip_connect | higher | Exp 28: gains of +16.6 to +44.9 |
| 5 | e5 → none | e4 = none | lower | Exp 63, 64: drops of −6.6 to −75.3 |
| 6 | e5 → none | e5 = nor_conv_3x3 | lower | Exp 61–64, 70 negative; Exp 65–67 near zero or positive |
| 7 | e3 → nor_conv_1x1 | e4 = none | higher | Exp 75, 78: gains of +27.3 to +75.8 |
| 8 | e3 → nor_conv_1x1 | e3 = none | higher | Exp 71, 75–79 beat Exp 72–74 |
| 9 | e4 → skip_connect | e3 = none | higher | Exp 34: +3.3 / +6.2 / +13.1 |
| 10 | e1 → skip_connect | e3 = none | higher | Exp 57, 58: ImageNet16-120 +11.2 to +11.4 |

**Caveats:**
- Hypotheses 2, 3 and 4 each lean mainly on a single all-skip parent (Exp 9, 19, 28). They are supported by the general pattern, not by a balanced sample.
- Hypothesis 10 is driven almost entirely by ImageNet16-120. In Exp 57, CIFAR-100 actually moved the other way (−1.84). This makes "consistent across all three datasets" the least certain claim in the set.
